coreWitness.rationale: artifacts/input_claim.sha256 is stage_input's declared completion artifact, but it holds only the SHA-256 of the frozen claim, which the planner cannot independently derive and no expectation type can express. The claim bytes (artifacts/input_claim.txt) and the model outputs (verdict.json, report.md) are fully witnessed. This is a repairable in-scope artifact gap: retarget stage_input's completion to artifacts/input_claim.txt so the produced claim bytes are independently assertable; see the blocking pipeline-artifact finding.

findings.summary: stage_input completion gates on a digest file whose exact bytes cannot be independently asserted by the Trial planner; retarget the completion to artifacts/input_claim.txt.
findings.evidence: quick_verify/quick_verify.yaml task factcheck.stage_input has completion {type: file_exists, path: artifacts/input_claim.sha256}. The Host derives the task's declared core artifact from that completion path and requires a concrete content expectation for it, but the file holds only the SHA-256 of the current claim (write_claim.py writes digest+'\n'). The planner cannot independently derive that 64-hex digest, and no expectation type expresses it: file-equals/file-contains need literal bytes, json-pointer-equals/json-pointer-text-occurrence need a JSON field, and file-source-text-occurrence needs a JSON source. validate confirms: adding the digest file to generatedInputPaths yields 'requires file-equals or present:true file-source-text-occurrence sourcePath evidence', and removing it yields 'Every declared core artifact must have a concrete content expectation'. The claim bytes themselves (artifacts/input_claim.txt) ARE independently assertable, so pointing the completion at artifacts/input_claim.txt (leaving the digest as an internal scratch file consumed by validate_verdict.py) would let the core be witnessed and remove this blocker.
